items.text: In client dairy herds of one veterinary practice, can facilitated biosecurity planning visits delivered by the herd's own vet be delivered as planned, and do they increase the number of observed core biosecurity measures in place at six months?
items.population: Client dairy herds of the practice whose farmers agree to take part
items.intervention: Facilitated planning visit with three agreed farm-specific priorities and a follow-up call
items.comparator: Measures observed at baseline in the same herds
items.outcome: Number of five core measures observed in place at six months; proportion of visits delivered as planned

finer: Feasible within two vets' half-days; interesting to the practice and farmers; novel locally; ethical with farmer consent and no animal procedures; relevant because advice is currently not followed.
summary: One implementation question on delivery and observed adoption.
